nodes.line: Keep walking. Don't look at the cooling towers. Everyone looks at the cooling towers. That's how they sort you.

options.label: Ask about the server farms
options.response: Every camera in the Union phones home here. The footage never leaves. Nothing here ever leaves. Including some of the staff.

options.label: Ask about a routing cover sheet
options.response: A paper cover sheet? Retro. I found one in Building 7's recycle queue. Downloading it to paper now. Do not ask what else was in the queue.

options.label: Mention the Form 27-B you are definitely not filling in
options.response: A paper form? Here? That's adorable. I've already queued it for archival. By mentioning it, you filed it.

options.label: Report in after orientation
options.response: The badge reader blinked twice when you walked up. That means you're on the roster. Or flagged. Same system.

options.label: Ask about the turnover
options.response: People rotate out. Contractors rotate in. The badges stay. The badges always stay.

options.label: Keep walking
options.response: We never spoke. But your gait is in the system now. Nothing personal. It's just good data.

options.label: Ask about the informant census
options.response: There's a headcount. There is no headcount. Sign in and visit every one of us — twelve of us, coast to coast — and the circuit owes you a badge. A plastic one. It's official.

options.label: Present your census card for a countersign
options.response: "Ping" scans it, signs the checksum. "Logged. Backed up. Deniable in three jurisdictions."

nodes.line: Building 7 hums louder than the others. Nobody's badge opens Building 7. Building 7 opens you, if you catch my drift.

options.label: Ask about Building 7
options.response: I've said too much. It's a cooling facility. For cooling. Say it back to me: a cooling facility.

options.label: Let it go
options.response: Good instinct. Curiosity is a metrics event here.

name: Clerk Miriam
role: Permits Desk, Office of Zoning Compliance

nodes.line: The desk is virtual. I am the desk. Your appointment expired in 2019. Would you like to reschedule it retroactively?

options.label: Ask about a ladder permit
options.response: Ladder permits are issued by the ladder permit office. This is the zoning desk. The ladder office is also me, on Tuesdays.

options.label: Ask about Form 27-B
options.response: 27-B is handled by the Bureau. The Bureau is everywhere. The Bureau is also me, on Wednesdays. Take this. Read nothing into it.

options.label: Present Boomer Dave's Form 12-F
options.response: A paper 12-F! Scanning... valid. Missing: one routing cover sheet. The cover sheet department is deprecated. Seek an unofficial channel. This desk denies saying that.

options.label: Submit the form for review
options.response: Processing... complete. Outstanding requirement: one (1) agent signature. Note: agent signatures are mythical. This is noted in the notes.

options.label: Present the signed Form 27-B
options.response: A genuine agent signature. I will stop asking how. The Bureau recognizes you. Take the stamp. It halves the paperwork of existence itself.

options.label: Ask where the forms are
options.response: The forms are online. The site is down. The outage notice is a form. You may fill it out online.

options.label: Abandon the desk
options.response: Your departure has been timestamped. Your arrival never was. You were never here, officially.

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Clerk Miriam stamps your card without looking up. 'Filed. Countersigned. Never happened. Next window.'

name: Boomer Greg
role: Angel Investor (Retired), Perpetual Motion Capital Lobby

nodes.line: I bought this place in '91 for two hundred grand and a firm handshake. Now the hedge funds pay ten million to live next to my lemon tree.

options.label: Ask about his startup
options.response: We put a modem in a toaster in 1999. Lost everything. Beautiful time to be alive. You kids with your cameras have no vision.

options.label: Ask about the street cameras
options.response: Fine by me. I sit on the porch and wave at them. Some kid in a warehouse gets paid to wave back. That's the economy.

options.label: Leave Greg to his lemons
options.response: Pull yourself up by your bootstraps. That's what the cameras are doing, incidentally.

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Boomer Greg signs in duplicate and keeps the carbon. 'Documented. Filed. Framed, probably. You're one of us now, kid.'

nodes.line: Thirty acres of lawn and not one blade out of place. The grass is monitored. The grass monitors back.

options.label: Ask about the grass
options.response: Sensors in the turf. Footsteps, weight, dwell time. I mow around them. They're sensitive. We have an understanding.

options.label: Ask about the mowing drones
options.response: They mow at night. I supervise. Supervising means I stand here so the drones see a human in charge. Morale purposes.

options.label: Ask about timesheet records
options.response: Ray's timesheets? Sure. The campus compost log doubles as an HR archive. Dug 'em out. They need an official stamp or HQ pretends paper isn't real. Good luck.

options.label: Step off the lawn
options.response: Good. The lawn logged you at an acceptable distance. Keep it that way.

options.label: Have Walt confirm the moat inflow
options.response: Walt wipes his hands. 'Datacenter coolant and one espresso machine's worth of drip. The campus drains its secrets downhill. Confirmed.'

options.label: Ask about the groundskeeper circuit
options.response: Six of us mow around the things nobody explains. Visit every groundskeeper, get the countersigns, and the circuit cuts you a master key.

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Groundskeeper Walt signs with a muddy thumb. 'Counted. The hatch keys talk to each other, you know. Now they'll know you.'

nodes.line: Surveillance is the last unpriced externality, bro. Every camera is a yield-bearing asset. I am long pigeons. Long, bro. LONG.

options.label: Ask about the fund
options.response: We securitize foot traffic. Bundle the crosswalks, tranche the jaywalkers, sell the alpha back to the city. It's basically free money. The city is the exit liquidity.

options.label: Ask about the cameras
options.response: Cameras? Bullish. Each unit is a data oil well. I tried to buy one off a guy once. He said they're not for sale. Everything is for sale, bro. He just didn't like my term sheet.

options.label: Ask about his losses
options.response: We don't say losses. We say 'pre-profit turbulence.' I was down 90% on artisanal pickle futures in Q2. Q3 I'm down 95%. That's called doubling your conviction.

options.label: Walk away mid-pitch
options.response: Your loss, bro! Actually it's alpha decay! I'll invoice you for the exposure!

options.label: Ask about the campus moat
options.response: I paid for a defensive moat. It's filling with something that isn't rainwater. Walt mows the whole valley — he knows what drains where. Confirm the inflow and I'll invoice someone.

options.label: Report the inflow to Brad
options.response: Brad nods like a man adding a line item. 'Coolant. In my moat. That's a licensing opportunity. You're on the friends-of-the-moat list.'

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Brad Kellerman initials in gel pen. 'Approved. Your account with the circuit is now... let's call it interest-bearing.'

nodes.line: Our moat is that nobody understands the product, including us. Comprehension is a liability. It creates doubt, and doubt is unhedgeable.

options.label: Ask about the moat
options.response: Patent pending. Trademark pending. Product pending. But the deck? The deck is READY, bro. Sixty slides of pure slope.

options.label: Nod like you understand
options.response: You get it. You don't get it. Same thing at our level. Welcome aboard. I'll have legal send you nothing.
